result.topic_en: Euler discusses flow through a very narrow middle tube BC between a wide upper vessel and a lower tube CD: the observed reduction in outflow velocity is attributed to friction, and the contraction of the water stream is accounted for by taking the effective length of BC greater and the heights of the adjoining tubes smaller.

items.quote:
Experimentis autem conſtat, ob
gracilitatem huiusmodi meatus medii BC celeritatem
effluxus non mediocriter imminui, vnde huius dimi-
nutionis cauſa aperte frictioni eſt tribuenda, cum ſubla-
ta frictione amplitudo huius tubi $gg$ celeritatem effluxus
non afficeret.
items.english: But it is established by experiments that, owing to the narrowness of such a middle passage BC, the velocity of outflow is considerably diminished; hence the cause of this diminution must clearly be attributed to friction, since with friction removed the width $gg$ of this tube would not affect the outflow velocity.

items.quote:
At ſi amplitudo tubi BC multo minor eſt,
quam ſuperioris et inferioris, euidens eſt, venam aquae,
quae ex vaſe ſuperiori in eum intrat, iam ante con-
trahi, ſimilique modo, cum inde in tubum ampliorem
CD egreditur, etiam nunc poſt egreſſum contractiorem
manere
items.english: But if the width of tube BC is much smaller than that of the upper and lower ones, it is evident that the stream of water entering it from the upper vessel is already contracted beforehand, and likewise, when it passes from there into the wider tube CD, it remains contracted even after leaving.

items.quote:
Quae circumſtantia in calculum inducetur,
ſi longitudo tubi gracilioris BC aliquanto maior aeſti-
metur, quam reuera eſt; atque tantumdem de altitudine
tuborum contiguorum dematur.
items.english: This circumstance will be brought into the calculation if the length of the narrower tube BC is estimated somewhat greater than it really is, and the same amount is subtracted from the height of the adjoining tubes.

items.quote:
Hinc ergo altitudo
$b$ eo maior eſt cenſenda, quo minor fuerit amplitudo
huius tubi, prae amplitudine tam ſuperioris, quam infe-
rioris.
items.english: Hence the height $b$ must be considered the greater, the smaller the width of this tube is compared with the width of both the upper and the lower one.
